rows.statement: Duty days for a team member generally run from the start of official pre-season training (training camp) through the team's last game, and include game days, practice days, team meetings, promotional events and post-season games; team travel days count in the total. States differ in detail.
rows.value: training camp + practices + meetings + games + postseason (travel days in the denominator)

rows.notes: Key jock-tax-duty-day-what-counts. CONFLICT/VARIATION: Arizona's rule starts duty days at the team's 1st regular-season game (pre-season training not listed as a duty-day category), while Massachusetts starts at the beginning of the official pre-season training period and Missouri expressly includes training camps. MA and AZ: travel days with no in-state game/practice/meeting are not in-state duty days but count in the total. MA excludes unpaid suspension days and presumes disabled-list days are not in-state unless rehab is done at the team's in-state facility. Tax Foundation 2003 report (older) said most states count only game days; superseded by current regs. Status: 6 independent sources (3 primary). rows.statement: A few states give nonresident employees a filing/withholding grace period: Illinois, Indiana and Montana allow 30 days; Louisiana, North Dakota, Utah and West Virginia offer limited reciprocal day-based relief that expressly excludes professional athletes and entertainers; Connecticut and Maine use combined day-and-income tests; nine states use dollar thresholds.
